name: Nomadic Civilizations
purpose: A starting subject map for a Nomadic Civilizations YouTube channel. Categories organize concrete subtopics; each entry supplies an episode question, a research outline and a boundary for case selection. Counts follow the authored coverage, with no imposed topic maximum.

topics.title: Mongol seasonal mobility
topics.question: Mongol seasonal mobility: what do contemporary records establish, and what remains uncertain?
topics.coverage: Primary context: Nomadic Civilizations; branch: Pastoral societies. Address Mongol seasonal mobility through one bounded case, source set or experiment. Exclude an all-purpose survey of the whole niche; distinguish the case's findings from broader claims.
research_outline: Locate Mongol seasonal mobility in a bounded time and place; build a chronology from identified records.
Compare at least two independent witnesses or explain why only one survives.
Analyze institutions, material conditions and overlooked participants rather than attributing everything to a single figure.
Separate documented conclusions, interpretive debates and gaps that a reconstruction cannot resolve.

history.requirements: Compare dated primary records, material evidence and historical scholarship. Distinguish event dates, the dates of surviving witnesses, later retellings and disagreement. Do not invent quotations, intentions or an unbroken lineage.
source_leads: dated archival records and original publications
inscriptions, artifacts or photographs with provenance

community.requirements: Use consented participant accounts, local records and the community's own descriptions. Include differences of position, access and power; testimony is not a representative survey or clinical proof.
source_leads: field notes with method and consent documented

overlap_policy: The following homes have deliberately related subject matter. They are navigation leads, not proof that the same question belongs in every bank. Choose one primary home for an actual episode and link it elsewhere. Where a subject appears in more than one context, retain the distinct case, population, system or interpretive question.

handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.
